transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because no matter what anyone says, I know some people at work are secretly working together to set me up, and nobody seems to take that seriously. It’s incredibly frustrating that everyone else just brushes it off as if I'm imagining things when I know exactly what they are doing.
Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you think that your coworkers are plotting against you, and have you experienced any other unusual thoughts or beliefs lately?

It started when a senior driver publicly challenged my authority, and now he, a few other drivers, and an outside maintenance contractor are leaving critical details off the paperwork on purpose to set me up for a future accident. I don't have any other "unusual" thoughts or issues going on; this is a very specific, real threat to my job and my reputation.
How long have you been noticing these behaviors from your coworkers and the maintenance contractor, and have your beliefs about their intentions changed or evolved over time?

This has been going on for about a year, starting right after that driver publicly challenged me following the bus collision incident. At first, I just started checking the inspection logs more closely, but over the months it became completely clear that they are actively coordinating to make it look like I signed off on unsafe buses.

You've mentioned this has been going on for about a year, but can you tell me if your belief about their plot has become more detailed or complex over time, or has it remained relatively the same since you first started noticing it?

It has definitely become more detailed as I've uncovered more of what they're doing. It started with just that one driver, but over the months I noticed clear patterns in the logs proving an outside maintenance contractor was also in on it. Now, I have to obsessively document every single detail of my inspections just to protect myself from their setup.

Have you experienced any other symptoms such as hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or feeling like your thoughts are being controlled or broadcasted to others at any point during this past year?

No, absolutely not, I don't hear voices, see things, or feel like my thoughts are being controlled or anything like that. My mind is completely clear, and my only concern is the very real plotting and sabotage that's happening to me at work.
Have you ever had a period, no matter how brief, where you questioned the reality of this plot against you or considered the possibility that your coworkers might not be out to get you?

No, I have never doubted it for a second because the evidence is just too clear and consistent to be a coincidence. It is impossible for this to be a mistake when the exact same group of people are repeatedly leaving things off the logs. I am absolutely certain they are trying to set me up.
Have you noticed any significant distress or impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning as a result of your beliefs about the plot against you?

Outside of this specific issue at work, my day-to-day life is completely normal—I still do my job by the book, pay my bills, and spend time with my brothers like I always have. However, it has caused some tension at work, as staff meetings have gotten really tense, some drivers avoid talking to me, and my supervisor had to pull me aside because I get so worked up over the safety reports.

Have you ever experienced a period where your belief in the plot was interrupted, even briefly, by a time when you didn't think about it or didn't believe it was happening, or has it been constant since you first became aware of it?

No, it has been completely constant and uninterrupted ever since it first started a year ago. I haven't had any breaks or doubts about it because the threat is always there when I'm at work. I am completely sure they are still actively trying to set me up every single day.
Have you ever felt like your belief about the plot against you is something that you can't control or stop thinking about, even when you try to focus on other things or distract yourself?

I don't see it as an uncontrollable thought that I want to stop, but rather as a very real threat that I am forced to focus on to protect myself. While I do spend a lot of time and energy poring over the logs at work, I can easily distract myself and enjoy normal things, like hanging out with my brothers on weekends, when I am away from the job.

Have you ever had any episodes, no matter how brief, where you experienced a complete break from reality, such as believing you were someone else, or having thoughts that were completely disconnected from your plot beliefs, or has your belief in the plot been the only unusual thought you've had?

No, I've never had anything like a break from reality or thought I was someone else; my mind is completely clear and normal. This situation with my coworkers setting me up is the only unusual thing I've had to deal with. Outside of protecting myself from this plot, my life and my thoughts are completely ordinary.

The patient's preoccupation with the plot is significant and causes distress and impairment in their occupational functioning, but their thoughts and behaviors are focused and goal-directed, which is more consistent with a delusional disorder. Therefore, F22 is the most likely candidate at this point.
